title: The exhibition that amazed a century
text: The Great Exhibition {{1}} held in Hyde Park in 1851, housed {{2}} a vast palace of glass and iron bolted together in a matter of months. The Crystal Palace, {{3}} was itself the greatest marvel of the show, displayed fourteen thousand exhibits from around the world, ranging {{4}} machine tools and locomotives to silks and the Koh-i-Noor diamond. {{5}} attracted some six million visitors in five months — about a fifth of the population of Britain — and the ticket receipts turned the venture into {{6}} triumph. The profits, {{7}} were invested in South Kensington, funded the natural history and science museums that still stand there, in a district nicknamed {{8}} Albertopolis after the prince who championed the idea.
